== Information ==
Damage charts are a common table found in multiple actors. It determines how an enemy should react when hit with various attacks, allowing for a great deal of customization. 

== Structure ==

The damage chart is a structure that is 0x20 bytes long. Each byte within the damage chart stores info on being hit by a particular attack (or attack group).

 & 0F = Damage
 & F0 = Effect Type //The effect of any value is actor dependent.

===Example===
Let's look at a Deku Baba
<pre>
DEKU BABA
10 02 01 02 E2 02 02 02 F1 F2 F4 24 02 02 02 02
02 24 00 00 00 00 F1 F4 F2 F2 F8 F4 00 00 04 00
</pre> 
The <tt>10</tt> byte stores the effect and damage that will occur when a Deku Baba is hit with a Deku Nut. The 1 digit is the effect that occurs when the Deku Baba is hit, which a stun effect in this case, while the 0 is the amount of damage the Deku Nut will deal. So the deku nut stuns it without doing any damage. Effect ids vary from enemy to enemy. For instance, the freeze effect id is 3 in a guay, but is 0xF in a tektite.

Arrows 6, 7, and 8 are not simply repeats of the fire arrow. The fire arrow animation may act as a place holder, but these arrows have their own damage mappings within the enemy damage charts. <br>
Also the 3 additional arrows don't use magic when used.<br>

==Item drops==
Like Likes only give the large purple rupee when defeated with light arrows. So? Well, all 3 beta arrows give unique items when used to defeat the like like.<br>

==Loading the arrows in-game==
The arrows can be loaded by modifying function 80834380 in {{actor ref|0000}}, or by execute breakpointing 80032458 in RAM and changing the variable before the ActorSpawn function is called.

==Finding damage charts in any actor==
A bit of knowledge of MIPS assembly helps to understand this part.

Finding the damage chart in RAM is quite easy; there is a pointer to it that is located 0x98 bytes after the start of the [[Actors#Loading_Actors|actor type lists]]. Finding the damage chart in ROM takes a little more effort.

First, get the assembly source of the actor you want. They can be found [http://spinout182.com/mqd/a here] for MQ Debug and [http://spinout182.com/mmde/a here] for MM Debug.

Once you have the actors' source (in assembly), look for the first <tt>jal</tt> to <tt>0x800FA958</tt> (for MM Debug) or <tt>0x8005C364</tt> for MQ Debug. Before the call to that function, you will see something like: <tt>lui t6 %(data_''offset'')</tt> - In MM Debug <tt>t6</tt> will not be the register, it will be <tt>a3</tt>. Regardless, <tt>data_''offset''</tt> will be the label of the damage chart of that enemy.

An alternate method (but mostly the same) can be seen [http://glitchkill.proboards.com/index.cgi?board=tuts2&action=display&thread=5879&page=1 here].
